headline: With the value on a plain inline style and the class fully static, `@yak/solid` folds and matches hand-written Solid at 2.16M renders/s — the control that isolates its CSS-variable path as the whole cost.

microbench.why: With no interpolation in the template the styled component folds to a plain element, so `yak-solid` reaches 2.16M renders/s against `vanilla-solid`'s 2.17M — a gap of half a percent, well inside the spread. `next-yak` at 1.56M does the same on React. `next-yak-nofold` at 1.12M is the price of keeping the wrapper for a component that has nothing dynamic left to do.

autocannon.why: `vanilla` at 1,190 req/s, `next-yak` at 1,170, `vanilla-solid` at 1,170 and `yak-solid` at 1,120 finish inside each other's spread — a four-way tie where the styling library has been compiled out of the request entirely.

attribution.why: `vanilla-solid` renders in 0.688 ms and `yak-solid` in 0.708 ms with 0.012 ms of lib and 0.255 ms of framework, against 11.3 ms with 9.58 ms of framework on the CSS-variable path. `next-yak` at 0.889 ms still books 0.238 ms of lib, so its fold leaves slightly more behind than yak-solid's does.

hydrate.why: `vanilla-solid` at 30.7 ms and `yak-solid` at 31.1 ms are indistinguishable, and both React lanes sit near 50 ms. With the element folded there is nothing of the library left for hydration to walk.

inp.why: `yak-solid` at 6.3 ms leads with `vanilla-solid` and `vanilla` at 7.5 ms — the narrowest spread of the trio, because with the value on an inline style the update is one attribute write for every lane.

mount.why: `vanilla-solid` mounts in 22.0 ms and `yak-solid` in 22.7 ms, roughly a third of the React lanes' 64 ms. A folded element with an inline style is DOM construction and nothing else.

renderTiming.why: One style recalculation per lane. An inline style never touches the sheet, so this is the cheapest shape a dynamic value can take for the style engine.

payload.why: `vanilla` at 5,502 gz B is the floor and `next-yak` adds 1,152 B of runtime. `yak-solid` at 11,852 B ships the smallest CSS in the case, 67 B, and the largest HTML, 8,073 B, which is Solid's hydration keys on a thousand dots.

nsweep.why: `yak-solid` holds 1.75 ms at 4,000 instances and `vanilla-solid` 1.84 ms, both flat. The same lane bends to 39.1 ms once the value goes through a CSS variable, which is the sharpest statement of the cost in the suite.

crossCase: The control for the Examples `dyn-translate` and `dyn-fair`. On React the CSS variable costs `next-yak` about half: 1.56M renders/s here against 792,000 there. On Solid it costs nineteen times: `yak-solid` reads 2.16M here and 113,000 there, with 0.255 ms of framework time in this case against 9.58 ms in the other. Same library, same value, and the only difference is whether the compiler could fold the element away.
